## Breaking change
* UI configurations are added to `apcupsd` integration, existing YAML configurations will be automatically imported except the configurations for the `binary_sensor` platform.


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

This PR refactors the `apcupsd` integration to use the config flow framework for better user experience and aligns with home assistant's goals. It also removes YAML config support as directed by architectural decision record (let me know if this is too aggressive and we should first deprecate it). Tested on my APC UPS.

Also, this is my first PR to home assistant, feel free to point out where I did was wrong 😃 

Other code quality changes such adding more tests / type hints will happen in separate PRs after this is merged.

@emontnemery 
> Please add an import flow of the YAML config to not make this a breaking change.
> 
> If an import flow is not possible, please explain why.

I was trying to implement import flow for this, but found a problem.

The yaml config looks like the following:

```yaml
apcupsd:
  host: localhost
  port: 1234

sensor:
  - platform: apcupsd
     resources:
       - abc
       - efg
       - ....
```

This PR implements the resource filter (`resources` config) as options, so users can select/deselect which resources they want to integrate into HA, this works great for `sensors`. However, `apcupsd` also exposes a `binary_sensor` that is tied to `STATFLAG` resource. In the YAML config you can simply not adding `binary_sensor` section to hide it, so we cannot simply import this behavior (`async_setup_platform` is not even called).

Another thing is `binary_sensor` also has a `name` field, which I think now is deprecated and users should instead configure the name of entities via UI? Do we want to import this as well or is it fine for this kind of "small" breaking changes?

BTW is there a guide on implementing import flows to set options? I tried to call `hass.config_entries.options.async_init` (or `hass.config_entries.async_update_entry`) in `sensor`'s `async_setup_platform` to update the `resources` options, but it's giving me weird bugs that seem like race conditions:

```
  File "/core/homeassistant/config_entries.py", line 466, in async_unload
    result = await component.async_unload_entry(hass, self)
  File "/core/homeassistant/components/binary_sensor/__init__.py", line 173, in async_unload_entry
    return await component.async_unload_entry(entry)
  File "/core/homeassistant/helpers/entity_component.py", line 172, in async_unload_entry
    raise ValueError("Config entry was never loaded!")
ValueError: Config entry was never loaded!
```

```
 File "/core/homeassistant/config_entries.py", line 327, in async_setup
    result = await component.async_setup_entry(hass, self)
  File "/core/homeassistant/components/sensor/__init__.py", line 210, in async_setup_entry
    return await component.async_setup_entry(entry)
  File "/core/homeassistant/helpers/entity_component.py", line 157, in async_setup_entry
    raise ValueError("Config entry has already been setup!")
ValueError: Config entry has already been setup!
```

I added an artificial sleep before `hass.config_entries.options.async_init` and the errors disappear, I'm guessing I have to wait for platforms to be fully set up before I can update the options in the config entry (since it will trigger a config reload, which in turn will trigger a re-setup)? But I'm not completely sure... [this](https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&rct=j&q=&esrc=s&source=web&cd=&ved=2ahUKEwjjwo7J48v1AhXEc98KHW0BBeoQFnoECAUQAQ&url=https%3A%2F%2Fcommunity.home-assistant.io%2Ft%2Fconfig-flow-import-set-options%2F198492&usg=AOvVaw2nQKToh7ZeeGO6W2ZyTop4) is the most related article I can find but it does not mention bugs like this....

OK I think I have found a workaround for the above issue. We should actually set up the config entry (`hass.config_entries.flow.async_init`) when we have all the information (`host`, `port` and `resources`). 

So when we set up the integration we temporarily store the `host` and `port` information in `hass.data[DOMAIN]` with a special entry ID `SOURCE_IMPORT` (to avoid conflicts with existing entry IDs). Later when sensor platform is set up, we gather the `resources` field and from there we import the config entry. The config flow is also updated to import extra `CONF_RESOURCES` field in `user_input` as options as well (though it does not show in the form). It's indeed a bit hacky but once we fully deprecate YAML config in the near future it's not hard to remove this.

Tested locally and it works great. This PR is now ready for review with a caveat: the YAML config for `binary_sensor` is not imported (should we log a warning?) because of the workaround, but it only has a `name` field which can be easily configured through UI I think....

## The problem
The apcupsd polling is too high (like 60 seconds) and i can't see a power failure if power turn on quickly. is a good thing enable the user to set the polling time or set it with a low value like 2-3 seconds.

i think the polling value are this: `MIN_TIME_BETWEEN_UPDATES = timedelta(seconds=60)`

i'm using low polling value on my apcupsd server config and all works fine (for years)

I am using APCUPSD on my Raspberry Pi 4 running Home Assistant Core.
[Install Home Assistant Core](https://www.home-assistant.io/installation/raspberrypi#install-home-assistant-core)
[How to connect your APC UPS to Rpi and Home Assistant using apcupsd!](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/how-to-connect-your-apc-ups-to-rpi-and-home-assistant-using-apcupsd/10609)

 I was able to get 10 second polling by performing the following:
1. Update apcupsd.conf and set POLLTIME to 10 (default is 60) then restart the apcupsd service
`sudo nano /etc/apcupsd/apcupsd.conf`
`sudo service apcupsd stop`
`sudo service apcupsd start`

2. Modify the source for the APCUPSD component to reduce the minimum time between updates.
`cd /srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/homeassistant/components/apcupsd`
`sudo nano __init__.py`
Change `MIN_TIME_BETWEEN_UPDATES = timedelta(seconds=60)` to `MIN_TIME_BETWEEN_UPDATES = timedelta(seconds=10)`

3. Add `scan_interval: 10` to your configuration YAML.
Example:
```
- platform: apcupsd
    scan_interval: 10
    resources:
      - apc
      - date
```

I haven't done any development for Home Assistant before so I'm not sure I can add this feature officially. I will try when I have time. Hope this helps someone!
